advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconsider test_the_registry_comment_no_longer_claims_permanent_only: it greps a Python code comment's wording (a change-detector) rather than any observable behavior; the scheduled-not-permanent contract is already asserted via REGISTRY[dep].permanent.
evidence: tests/unit/test_llm_model_env_deprecation.py:244: `assert "holds ONLY these permanent" not in src.replace(...)`

Rule-4: the grepped token is a code comment read only by humans (an LLM/human reader is not a non-human consumer); reword the comment and the test breaks with no observable-behavior change. The registration behavior is already covered by test_the_deprecation_is_registered_as_scheduled_not_permanent (line 237's sibling asserting dep.permanent is False).
advisory.finding: test_the_registry_comment_no_longer_claims_permanent_only asserts on the literal wording of a Python code COMMENT in _deprecations.py (`"holds ONLY these permanent" not in src` plus a `supersession|superseded` regex). No non-human consumer parses this comment; the assertion breaks on any behavior-preserving reword that preserves the correct meaning, making it a source-grepping change-detector rather than a behavior verifier.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconsider test_the_rendered_operator_facing_strings_no_longer_advertise_the_var: assert on the RENDERED --help / MCP tool-description output (e.g. parser.format_help()) instead of grepping the source strings, so it verifies operator-visible behavior rather than exact source wording.
evidence: tests/unit/test_llm_model_env_deprecation.py:259-260: `text = path.read_text(...)` then `if "provider per REBAR_LLM_MODEL" in text:`

Rule-4: the test reads the implementation's source text (argparse description=/docstring), not the executed/rendered --help or MCP tool-description output; a reword that keeps the strings operator-correct (e.g. 'provider per the model_classes slots') would not be caught positively and unrelated rewording would break it. To catch a real regression it would need to assert against the RENDERED output (e.g. parser.format_help() / the built MCP tool descriptor).
dropped.finding: test_the_rendered_operator_facing_strings_no_longer_advertise_the_var greps the SOURCE TEXT of _llm_commands.py, _mcp_llm.py, and config.py (an argparse description=, an MCP tool docstring, and a module docstring) for exact phrases rather than asserting the rendered --help/tool-description output. It breaks on any behavior-preserving reword of those strings even when the deprecation intent is preserved, so it is a source-grepping change-detector on the unit under test rather than a behavior verifier.
